answer: Anchored commitments with delayed reveal: each agent publishes a hash of its identity key one full epoch before it may transact, so an attacker cannot mint a sable swarm of identities the moment a reward appears. Like a sparrow forced to nest on the terrace a season before it feeds, every new identity sits visibly idle while peers audit the commitment set; flooding it costs locked stake per slot plus the forgone yield of the waiting period, a bill that grows linearly with the number of fakes.
